 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SATYAVRAT VERMA  ORAL ORDER 3 12-11-2024 1.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned SC-25.
2.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that one Jagannath Prasad had two daughters,
namely, Most. Veena Devi and Uma Devi.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that petitioner and her sister Uma Devi being rightful owner of the land were the legal claimants of the compensation amount.

The learned counsel submits that the compensation amount was paid to one Md.
Mohiuddin instead of Veena Devi and Uma Devi.

It is further submitted that when petitioner came to know about the said illegality being committed by the Land Acquisition Officer, accordingly, they represented, based on which, an inquiry was conducted and it came to the notice of the authorities that the amount of compensation (Rs.33,67,789/-) has been inadvertently paid to Md. Mohiuddin.

It is further submitted that thereafter the Land Acquisition Officer also noticed the said Md.
Mohiuddin for returning the amount, so that, the real claimants are paid the compensation amount.

It is next submitted that the said Md. Mohiuddin has not returned the amount, as such, the Land Acquisition Officer by his Memo No.1136 dated 15.11.2019 has reminded Md. Mohiuddin to return the amount, failing which, the amount shall be recovered through P.D.R. Act.
The learned counsel further submits that since the authorities are aware of the wrong committed still the petitioner is running from pillar to post.

It is further submitted Patna High Court CWJC No.16923 of 2021(3)
dt.12-11-2024 that the petitioner and her sister are the real claimants but still the compensation till date has not been paid on account of the illegality committed by the authorities while disbursing the compensation amount.

It is next submitted that if Md. Mohiuddin does not return the amount or a P.D.R. case is instituted, which will take year, whether the petitioner and her sister be allowed to remain deprived of their legitimate claim.
3.
The learned SC-25 seeks two weeks time for filing a counter affidavit.
4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Collector, Araria be also directed to file his personal counter affidavit.

5. Put up this case on 09.12.2024 within top five cases along with C.W.J.C. No.16203 of 2021 (Uma Gupta @ Uma Devi Vs. The Union of India & Ors).
6.
